author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ukraine is preparing for U.S.-mediated trilateral talks with Russia to resume in October, a senior Ukrainian official said Saturday, signaling a possible restart of diplomacy after months without a three-party meeting. Kyrylo Budanov, chief of staff to President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, described the planned discussions as an effort to address a war now more than four and a half years old.

The last trilateral meeting took place in Geneva in February. More recent visits by U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv have renewed diplomatic activity, and Zelenskiy has said Ukraine received proposals that could support another round. Possible host countries mentioned by the Ukrainian side include Turkey, the United Arab Emirates and Switzerland.

No date or venue has been finalized. The Kremlin has said Russia is open to renewed talks, while also saying the timing and location remain unsettled. Major disagreements continue, including the status of the Donbas region and other territory occupied or claimed by Russia. The announcement therefore represents preparation for negotiations, not an agreement on terms or a ceasefire. Developments in the coming weeks will show whether the tentative October timetable becomes a confirmed meeting.
dek: A senior Ukrainian official said planning is underway, though no date or venue has been finalized and core territorial disputes remain.
headline: Kyiv prepares for October resumption of U.S.-mediated talks with Russia
